endorsements.quote: Thus, a Data Partnerships Committee (DPC) was established to deal with issues relating to collaboration for innovation, and all activity was approved by the DPC.
We advocate establishment of a formal process that includes appropriate senior information governance staff responsible for compliance with data regulations.

unlisted_practices: Establish a national-level, single appraisal process, or at minimum guidance and templates, for data partnership and collaboration agreements between the NHS and industry.
Use anonymised data (defined according to ICO guidance) for industry-NHS partnerships wherever possible, within a secure data environment meeting appropriate security standards.
Share code and tooling developed from NHS data under open licences for reuse across the sector rather than commercialising intellectual property.
Give industry partner staff working in NHS organisations honorary contracts with associated training and onboarding so they are bound by the same governance processes.
Provide significant additional support and resourcing for NHS ICT teams to implement cloud infrastructure.
Provide dedicated funded clinical staff time and clinical research informatics officer and innovation officer roles representing all directorates to support innovation engagement.
Appoint dedicated project managers and use shared project management tooling with agreed escalation routes for NHS-industry partnerships.
Establish clinical-grade secure data environments and cloud infrastructure to support AI development and deployment pipelines outside proprietary EHR tools.
Engage NHS ICT early and provide dedicated ICT support functions for industry partnerships.
Establish specific workforce roles responsible and accountable for deployment, maintenance and governance of AI tools and infrastructure.

screen.reason: Brief report describing lessons learned and recommendations/governance frameworks from an industry-NHS collaboration preparing infrastructure and staff for AI and health data use.
